subject: general
question: The cost price of a box of marker is ₹3,300. The shopkeeper gives 75% of discount on the cost price. What will be the selling price (in ₹)?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Discount = 75% ⇒ Selling price = 25% of cost price

25% of 3300 = 3300 ÷ 4

= 825

No need for long calculation

**∴ Answer = 825**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Cost price = 3300, Discount = 75%

**Formula used:**

Selling Price = Cost Price − Discount

**Calculation:**

⇒ Discount = 75% of 3300

⇒ = (75 ÷ 100) × 3300

⇒ = 2475

⇒ Selling Price = 3300 − 2475

⇒ = 825

**∴ The correct answer is 825.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Discount Formula

Discount = (Discount% × Cost Price) ÷ 100

Selling Price

SP = CP − Discount

Shortcut Concept

If discount = x%, then SP = (100 − x)% of CP

Fraction Conversion

25% = 1/4, so divide by 4 directly
